documents.unit: Office of the Provost (Policy Office / Office of the Secretary)
documents.title: Policy 100-022: Howard University Artificial Intelligence (AI) Policy
documents.summary: Howard Policy 100-022 is a university-wide framework covering teaching, research, partnerships and work use. It sets no course-level AI rule: faculty set permissible use in syllabi and students ask when guidance is absent. Most of its content is data, IP and governance requirements.
documents.stance_why: The policy states that "Faculty shall establish and communicate, through course syllabi ... course requirements regarding the permissible and impermissible use of AI tools" and that students shall "seek clarification from the instructor" without course guidance, so it hands the decision to instructors.

units.why: This sets the institution-wide purpose: the policy exists "to ensure the responsible use of artificial intelligence" across academic, research and operational work. It is a framework preamble, so P56, actor all, informs.
units.anchor: to ensure the responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI)

units.why: The policy "will be reviewed annually and updated as necessary", a review cycle held by the Responsible Officer; P54 fits, with admin as the actor.
units.anchor: This policy will be reviewed annually and updated as necessary

units.why: The rationale says AI "can enhance teaching and learning" when "used responsibly", a framing of AI as beneficial with conditions; P56 (framework principle) fits better than P44 because it is not about professional skill.
units.anchor: can enhance teaching and learning, support research and scholarship

units.why: The rationale names risks "related to bias, accuracy, accessibility, privacy, data security, intellectual property"; this names harms (P53) and also touches privacy and IP, but P53 is the best single home because it lists bias and risks generally.
units.anchor: AI also presents risks related to bias, accuracy, accessibility, privacy, data security

units.why: The rationale states the policy "establishes a University-wide framework for the responsible use of AI" that "upholds academic integrity"; a scope and principles statement, P56.
units.anchor: establishes a University-wide framework for the responsible use of AI

units.why: The scope clause says the policy "applies to all members of the Howard University community, including faculty, staff, students"; scope definition, P61 (defines what the policy covers).
units.anchor: applies to all members of the Howard University community

units.why: Defines AI as systems that "perform tasks normally requiring human intelligence"; a definition setting scope, P61.
units.anchor: computer-based systems or software that perform tasks normally requiring human intelligence

units.why: Defines generative AI as systems that "generate new content, including text, images, audio, video, code"; code is explicitly in scope, P61.
units.anchor: AI systems designed to generate new content, including text, images, audio, video, code
units.frag_end: in response to user inputs or prompts.

units.why: Defines AI Tools as applications that "utilize artificial intelligence, including generative AI"; scope definition, P61.

units.why: Defines Responsible Use as "ethical, transparent, lawful" use with "safeguards to mitigate bias, protect privacy, and ensure human accountability"; a principles definition, P56 rather than P61 because it sets normative content.
units.anchor: ethical, transparent, lawful, and aligned with University policies
